use_when: To pick one value from a list of five or more, such as the property filter "All properties" on the back office calendar, or "Who" in the activity log filters.
Use size md (36px) in forms and for the sort control on search results; use size sm (30px) in compact filter bars and table headers.
Show the label above the field in forms. Hide it (ShowLabel off) only when the value says what it is, such as "Sort: Price, low first".
Always show a value in the field: the current choice or a neutral default such as "All properties". Never leave it blank.
Order options in a way people expect: by frequency, by time, or alphabetically, and put "All" first.
Keep option text short enough for one line at the field's width.

dont_use_when.when: For two to four options that should stay visible: use Buttongroup type segmented, or Radiocard.
To pick several values at once: use Chip filters or Checkboxes instead.
For actions such as "Export" or "Delete": use Button, or a Buttongroup.

variant_intent.md: forms and the sort control on search results (36px)
variant_intent.sm: compact filter bars and table headers (30px)

a11y.fact: The field is a native <button type="button"> with aria-haspopup="listbox", so focus and disabled behaviour are the browser's own.
aria-expanded reflects whether the menu is open, and aria-controls points at the listbox only while it is open.
With the label shown, the button is named by the label and its own value (aria-labelledby); with showLabel off, the label text is kept as aria-label.
The open menu is a role="listbox" named by the label (aria-labelledby, or aria-label when the label is hidden).
Each option is a role="option" with aria-selected, and the keyboard-active option is exposed through aria-activedescendant on the button.

Keyboard: ArrowDown/ArrowUp open the menu and move the active option, Home/End jump to the first/last, Enter or Space choose, Escape closes, and Tab closes; focus returns to the button after choosing.
